passage:
So it started with one post. I said something I thought was ordinary, and within a day strangers were tearing into me. I'm Chinmay, and my first instinct was to keep it quiet, because I felt ashamed even though I hadn't done anything terrible.

On day two I told Mum and Papa at the dinner table. I said, "I need you to know what's happening online, I don't want to handle it alone." Then I told two close friends. Abhinav offered right away: "Give me your login for a few days, I'll watch the comments so you don't have to." I set a rule that I'd only look at messages if he flagged them.

I slept for the first time in three nights. I'm not sure it fixed anything, but I wasn't alone in it.

qa.q: Who did Chinmay tell first at home?
qa.a: Chinmay told Mum and Papa at the dinner table.

qa.q: What might Chinmay have been feeling before telling anyone?
qa.a: Chinmay felt ashamed and isolated, wanting to keep it quiet even though nothing terrible had been done.

qa.q: What could Chinmay do if the comments turned into threats, and why?
qa.a: Chinmay could ask Mum and Papa to help save the messages and report them to the authorities, because serious threats need more than friends watching.

qa.q: How might Abhinav feel about being trusted with the login?
qa.a: Abhinav probably feels responsible and glad to help, and reading the comments so Chinmay does not have to is a real act of care.

grounding: The student tells parents and two close friends what is happening and asks a friend to monitor accounts, easing isolation.

I'm Jatin, Kunal's roommate. When the thread about his debate clip exploded, he went silent for a day, lying on his bed with the phone.
On the second evening he sat up and made calls, one after another, and I heard all of it. First his parents, on video. He showed them the worst comments and said, "I didn't want to worry you, but I'm not sleeping." His mother said they'd call every night that week, and his father told him to go to the student welfare office in the morning. Then he rang two old school friends.
Then he turned to me. "Can you keep an eye on my accounts till Sunday? Tell me only if something is a threat."
He handed me his login. That night he slept eight hours. I don't know what was going on in his head, but he looked lighter.

qa.q: Until when did Kunal ask Jatin to watch the accounts?
qa.a: He asked Jatin to keep an eye on them till Sunday.

qa.q: What does Kunal's first day lying silently on the bed suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt alone and overwhelmed, not ready to talk to anyone while the thread grew.

qa.q: What else could Kunal do to share the load?
qa.a: He could take his father's advice and visit the student welfare office, so trained staff know what is happening.

qa.q: How does the arrangement look to Jatin?
qa.a: Jatin is trusted with Kunal's login and a clear job, and notices Kunal seemed lighter, though Jatin cannot know his thoughts for sure.

grounding: Shows the student telling parents and friends about the pile-on and asking a friend to watch the accounts for a few days, easing isolation.

Monday. Tanuja didn't go to the canteen. Her post about the college dress code had drawn hundreds of angry comments, and she spent the day under a blanket, reading every one and telling no one.
Wednesday. She called home. "Mummy, Papa, I need to tell you something." She read them some comments. Mummy said, "You're not alone in this. We'll call each evening." Papa asked if any were threats. There weren't. That afternoon she met Chandrika and another close friend, Ifra, at the library steps and told them everything. She asked Chandrika, "Can you check my accounts for me till the weekend and only tell me if something's serious?" Chandrika took her phone and logged out of the app for her.
Saturday. Tanuja went to the canteen with Ifra. She hadn't opened the app in three days, and she laughed at a joke for the first time that week.

qa.q: Where did Tanuja meet Chandrika and Ifra?
qa.a: She met them at the library steps.

qa.q: How did Tanuja feel on Monday, and what shows it?
qa.a: She felt alone and overwhelmed, spending the day under a blanket reading every comment and telling no one.

qa.q: What else could Tanuja add to her plan?
qa.a: She could also let the college counsellor know, so an adult on campus is aware if the comments turn into threats.

qa.q: How might Chandrika feel being asked to check the accounts?
qa.a: Chandrika may feel trusted and a little protective, taking the phone and logging out of the app for Tanuja.

grounding: Shows the student telling parents and close friends about a pile-on and asking a friend to monitor the accounts, which reduces isolation.
